answer: Latency triangulation: each epoch, ten randomly chosen verifiers ping every agent and time the replies. Signals in fibre can't travel faster than light, so round-trip times pin each identity to a rough region, as fixed as basalt. Identities that triangulate to the same grove of servers share one reward cap, so 1,000 keys on one rack earn as a single agent. To dodge it, an attacker must rent machines in genuinely separate regions and pay full hosting for each, every epoch, which pushes a sybil farm off the profitable ledge.
